title: The Best New Gadgets and Hi-Fi Releases of 2026 (Updated)
summary: Including Audiolab's entry-level CD player, Noble Audio's latest hi-fi headphones and Kodak's neat AirTag alternative.

Learn more Including Audiolab’s entry-level CD player, Noble Audio’s latest hi-fi headphones and Kodak’s neat AirTag alternative. We’re already nearing the end of November and, naturally, a lot of new tech and gadgets have been announced since the start of the year. Of course, the product release cycle keeps on keepin’ on, so actually keeping track of every new gadget and hi-fi release is a tall order for even the most dedicated enthusiast. Catch up below and don’t forget to bookmark for later. This is a rolling list and is routinely updated throughout the year. Kodak Kodak SlideTag The SlideTag is a Bluetooth tracker compatible with Apple’s Find My network, so it works like an AirTag. But it’s designed to look like a 1935 Kodachrome slide mount. It features a 1.54-inch e-ink display that can be programmed to show a gallery of up to 12 digital photos. Basically, it functions as a little digital picture frame that you can attach to a keychain. The SlideTag comes in nine different retro designs, but Kodak is selling them in a “blind box” format. So when you order one, you don’t exactly know which one you’re going to get until you open it. read more $35 at Kodak Noble Audio Noble Audio Paladin Noble Audio’s Paladin is a high-end pair of in-ear monitors (IEMs) that are wrapped in shining armor, literally. They get their name from a paladin, a medieval knight, and have a distinctive appearance meant to look like chainmail. It consists of a woven pattern of small, interlocking rings with silver-finished resin shells. Inside, the Paladin IEMs are certified audiophile-grade. Each earbud has a 12-driver tribrid configuration comprising eight balanced armatures, two Sonion bone-conduction drivers and two Super-Magnetic planar drivers. A multi-way passive crossover brings the three driver technologies together. read more $3,500 at Bloom Audio Audiolab Audiolab 3000A Audiolab’s 3000A is a stereo integrated amplifier with a Class A/B architecture, capable of delivering 35 watts (into 8 ohms) or 55 watts (into 4 ohms). It has a built-in moving-magnet phono stage, so it pairs well with a wide range of entry-level turntables. The British audio maker calls the 3000A the “natural partner” for the 3000CD CD player. read more $699 at Audiolab Audiolab Audiolab 3000CD The 3000CD is Audiolab’s most budget-friendly CD player to date (and the first new CD player that the brand has produced in over a decade). It’s capable of playing CDs, CD-Rs and CD-RWs. It features a 32-bit stereo DAC that uses ESS HyperStream architecture and jitter-management technology. It has analog outputs, making it easy to connect to an amplifier (like the 3000A). read more $699 at Audiolab Teenage Engineering Teenage Engineering EP/BC-1 The Teenage Engineering EP/BC-1 is the company’s first-ever CD player. It has an unconventional design that leaves the CD fully exposed while playing. It has numerous analog buttons and knobs, red LED displays, and digital VU meters, but it also gives you DJ-style controls such as beat detection with tempo sync out and speeding up or slowing down tracks. Additionally, it’s optimized to work as part of a modular system, connecting with other products in the brand’s Broadcast Series, including the EP-35 portable speaker. read more $329 at Teenage Engineering Pro-Ject Pro-Ject Amp Box S3 L Pro-Ject’s Amp Box S3 L is a compact stereo power amplifier that is effectively the slightly larger, but significantly more powerful sibling to the company’s Amp Box S3. It’s capable of delivering 80 watts (into 8 ohms) and 140 watts (into 4 ohms), and is an ideal partner for demanding loudspeakers and larger listening rooms. Since it’s a power amplifier only, Pro-Ject designed it with the same footprint to be paired with its Pre Box S3 preamplifier. read more Learn More Grado Labs Grado GW200 Grado’s GW200 is a pair of wireless headphones with an open-back design. As the next evolution of the brand’s previous models, the GW100 and GW100x, the GW200 has been upgraded with a new 44mm S driver and advanced Bluetooth 5.4 connectivity with support for high-resolution codecs: aptX Lossless, aptX Adaptive, aptX HD, aptX, AAC, and SBC. They also have improved battery life, promising upwards of 60 hours on a single charge. read more $329 at Grado Labs Fluance Fluance RT86 The Fluance RT86 is a semi-automatic, belt-drive turntable that sits just below the company’s flagship RT87. The main difference between the two is that, instead of the RT87’s dual-plinth design, the RT86 has a traditional single-plinth. However, other hardware, like the 9-inch carbon fiber tonearm with adjustable Vertical Tracking Angle (VTA) and the high-mass, 4.1-pound acrylic platter, is the same as the flagship. Additionally, Fluance lets you choose between two moving-magnet cartridges: Audio-Technica’s AT-VM95ML or Ortofon’s 2M Blue. read more $700 at Fluance $700 at Amazon Campfire Audio Campfire Audio Cascara Mk2 The Cascara Mk2 is the second-generation version of Campfire Audio’s original Cascara IEMs. They feature the 10mm dual-magnet dynamic driver, which the brand describes as being valued for its rich, warm transients, deep-reaching bass, real texture, and smooth, detailed highs. But they have an updated look and subtle tuning refinements to help deliver smoother high frequencies. read more $549 at Campfire Audio Quad Quad 3 Series (90 Collection) Quad’s 3 Series is a range of new hi-fi components designed to look like its classic 1960s components. Each pairs a grey chassis and front panel with orange accents and LED backlighting, while incorporating modern engineering. The range consists of four components: the 303 stereo power amplifier, the 33 preamplifier, the 3 integrated amplifier and the 3CDT CD transport. Now, with the 90 Collection , Quad is giving the entire range a new look with satin black finishes and bright green accents. According to the brand, the 90 Collection “draws upon the visual direction established by modern Quad design and fuses it with the established classic appeal.” read more Learn More Onkyo Onkyo HA-70 Onkyo’s HA-70 is a compact headphone amplifier that is designed to serve as the centerpiece of a premium personal hi-fi system. It has a fully balanced circuit architecture with dedicated DAC and amplifier stages for each audio channel. Onkyo says this design “enhances channel separation, minimizes unwanted noise and distortion, and delivers greater dynamic stability, clarity, and musical precision.” It has three gain settings, giving it the versatility to handle “virtually any” headphones, from ultra-sensitive IEMs to ultra-demanding, high-impedance headphones (up to 600 ohms). read more $650 at Onkyo Bose Bose QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen) (Ice Blue and Vanilla Cream) Bose’s QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen) are the brand’s more affordable pair of noise-canceling headphones in the brand’s QuietComfort range. Released in August 2026, they are positioned just below the brand’s flagship QuietComfort Ultra Headphones, which cost $449. As of November 2026, Bose has introduced them in a new two-tone finish: ice blue and vanilla cream. read more $219 at Bose $359 (39% off) Klipsch Klipsch Stratos HP-2 and HP-3 The Stratos HP-2 and HP-3 are Klipsch’s first pair of over-ear wired headphones in over a decade. Both are similar designed, with real wood earcups and feature copper-ring accents, Klipsch Heritage Twitchell grille cloth, and a protein-leather headband. The difference between the two is that the HP-2 is a closed-back headphone, while the HP-3 is a semi-open-back headphone. Both headphones are highly efficient and easy to drive, so they can work in a wide range of listening setups. Both aim to deliver full-range sound with very little distortion. read more $1,000 at Klipsch (HP-2) $1,200 at Klipsch (HP-3) Audiolab Audiolab 6000CDT MKII Audiolab’s 6000CDT MKII is the next-generation version of the 6000CDT CD transport, which has been around since 2018. It features a completely new CD mechanism, a revised servo control, reworked power architecture, a new custom transformer, and an upgraded master clock. Together, Audiolab says they allow the 6000CDT MKII to deliver quieter, faster and more consistent disc replay. The company describes it as a “natural partner” to its 6000A MKII integrated amplifier. read more at Audiolab Noble Audio Noble Audio Astrid Noble Audio’s Astrid is new midrange pair of wireless earbuds with active noise-cancellation. They are positioned between the brand’s Rex5 ($449) and flagship Prestige Encore II ($699). Staying true to the brand’s wireless earbud ethos, the Astrid features a three-driver hybrid design, which combines an 8.3mm dynamic driver, a 6mm planar driver, and a balanced armature in each earpiece. They support high-resolution Bluetooth codecs, including LDAC and aptX Adaptive. They also integrate Audiodo’s Person Sound and Equalizer technologies. read more $539 at Bloom Audio Coturn by Thorens Coturn by Thorens CT-Two Thorens and industrial design firm Coturn have teamed up to create a portable turntable à la Audio-Technica’s Sound Burger. The CT-Two has a built-in phono preamplifier, but no built-in speakers, meaning you have to use its line-in connection to hook it up to an amplifier or pair of active speakers. Or it can stream audio to Bluetooth speakers or headphones. It’s positioned as a high-end option compared to other portable turntables, with a precision-machined aluminum chassis and touch-sensitive controls. read more $682 at Coturn Acoustic Energy Acoustic Energy 500 Series (2026) Acoustic Energy has introduced a second generation of its 500 Series of loudspeakers, which sits below its flagship Corinium range. It is comprised of three models: one bookshelf speaker (AE500²), two floorstanding speakers (AE509² and AE520²) and a center channel (AE507²). By integrating the new range with new driver, crossover and bracing technologies derived from its Corimium range, the British hi-fi maker claims the new 500 Series has “taken a substantial step forward in openness, naturalness, and musical coherence.” read more at Acoustic Energy Audioengine White Oak Collection Audioengine has introduced The White Oak Collection, which comprises two of its compact powered speaker systems, the HD4 Next Gen and HD5, but they come with new white oak cabinets. They also feature copper tweed grilles and gold accents. According to the brand, the new White Oak option brings “together natural textures, warm real wood, metal accents, and carefully selected premium materials to create a coordinated look that complements all interior design settings.” read more $329 at Audioengine (HD4) $429 (23% off) $449 at Audioengine (HD5) Gadhouse Gadhouse Eric CD Player Gadhouse’s Eric is a new-age portable CD player, meaning it has a built-in battery and support for USB-C charging (which vintage Discmans lacked), as well as built-in Bluetooth so you can stream CDs to wireless headphones or speakers. It supports CD and HQCD playback and features anti-skip technology. It has tactile controls and a transparent display that lets you see the CD spin as it plays. It has two 3.5mm jacks for wired listening; you and a friend can share a wired listening experience. read more $85 at Gadhouse $130 at Gadhouse (Wesley Bundle) Sony Sony MDR-3R The Sony MDR-3R is a modern take on the brand’s original MDR-3 headphones that were released in 1979 and debuted alongside the Walkman TPS-L2 player. The MDR-3R retains the original lightweight, open-ear design and features swappable blue and orange ear pads, letting users switch based on their mood or preferences. The biggest change is they have of a USB-C jack to connect directly to today’s smartphones and laptops. The cable also features a line-in microphone and remote for calls and adjusting volume and playback. read more $60 at Sony $80 at Sony (Stranger Things Edition) Pro-Ject Pro-Ject Debut Carbon The Original Pro-Ject’s Debut Carbon “The Original” is a modern revival of the brand’s iconic Debut Carbon, released in 2012. It’s a minimalist belt-drive turntable with an 8.6-inch one-piece carbon-fiber tonearm and comes pre-equipped with Pro-Ject’s upgraded Pick It S2 moving-magnet (MM) cartridge. It lacks a built-in phono preamplifier, so you’ll have to add your own. The company claims that the Debut Carbon The Original represents “a return to the Debut roots of affordable hi-fi turntables that are constructed to hi-fi standards.” read more $649 at Pro-Ject $649 at Henley Audio Tivoli Audio Tivoli Audio Model One BT (Naturals Collection) The Naturals Collection introduces the Model One BT in four additional colors: Sage, Angora, Eucalyptus and Ginger. According to the brand, the new color palette “reflects a broader shift toward warmer, more organic interiors, where cool grays and stark whites are giving way to muted greens, creamy neutrals, and earthy tones.” Aside from the new look, the Model One BT remains the same. It’s a single mono speaker with a single 3-inch full-range driver. It supports Bluetooth streaming (no Wi-Fi) and a built-in AM/FM radio. It also has an auxiliary line input and a headphone jack. read more $200 at Tivoli Audio Coolgeek Coolgeek P1 The Colorado-based audio brand has created a gorgeous new-age portable cassette tape player: the P1. It features a CNC-machined aluminum frame and a transparent body that lets you see the cassette’s moving gears and reels in action. It supports both wired and wireless headphones (thanks to built-in Bluetooth), and charges via USB-C. read more $179 at Coolgeek $179 at Kickstarter Schiit Audio Schiit Magni 6 Schiit’s sixth-generation Magni headphone amplifier looks and works similarly to its predecessors, but it has more power and more features. Just like previous models, the Magni 6 has a current-feedback discrete design, full DC coupling and a 100-percent linear power supply. But Schiit claims it is more powerful (now 3 watts per channel) and has a lower noise floor. Plus, the Magni 6 has a switchable preamp output, making it easier to switch between headphones and a powered desktop speaker system. Basically, you no longer have to unplug the headphones completely. The amp-only model costs $99, while the amp/DAC model costs $169. read more Starts at $99 iFi Audio iFi UP Travel Max iFi’s UP Travel Max is a tiny Bluetooth transceiver and DAC that supports the latest high-quality Bluetooth codecs, including LDAC, aptX Lossless, and aptX Adaptive. It supports two-way Bluetooth with both transmit and receive modes. This lets you plug it into a car or boat stereo system and stream audio from your smartphone. Or, it allows you to stream audio from a device, like an in-flight entertainment system, to a pair of wireless headphones. iFi claims the UP Travel Max is the first travel adapter to be able to both send and receive CD-quality audio over Bluetooth, and “the only lossless in-flight adapter built on a true hi-fi architecture.” read more $129 at iFi audio Audioengine Audioengine Headphone Stand Audioengine’s first headphone stand, the aptly named Headphone Stand , is a hollow rectangular box with smooth, rounded edges. It’s made of real wood and wrapped in a premium walnut finish that’s designed to match its various desktop speakers. According to the brand, it “offers a convenient place to store over-ear headphones while complementing the furniture and audio gear around them.” read more $59 at Audioengine Camp Snap Camp Snap 8 Mini Camp Snap introduced a smaller, more affordable version of the CS-8 digital camcorder it released in 2025. Like its larger sibling, the CS-8 Mini is a digital camera capable of capturing video and designed to resemble the Super 8 film cameras from the 1970s. But the Mini is roughly half the size, and is more geared to fit kids’ hands. The CS-8 Mini also comes in more kid-friendly colors, including blue, green, orange and pink. read more $150 at Camp Snap Twelve South Twelve South Cablesnap 65w Twelve South’s Cablesnap 65w is a compact power adapter with an integrated USB-C cable that pulls out (up to 29 inches) and automatically retracts. The travel charger delivers up to 65 watts and has extra USB-C and USB-A ports, so it can charge up to three devices simultaneously from one outlet. And it comes with UK and EU adapters for traveling abroad. Available in three finishes: dune (white), coastal (blue) and slate (black). read more $50 at Amazon $50 at Twelve South Goldring Goldring Extract Stylus Cleaning Kit Goldring says its stylus cleaning kit “offers everything you need to keep your turntable cartridge stylus in pristine condition.” It consists of a magnifying lens, an anti-static stylus cleaning brush and a cleaning gel pot. The included magnifying lens provides 10x magnification, allowing you to closely inspect your stylus for damage or contamination. The anti-static stylus cleaning brush helps remove the dust and fluff that the stylus picks up with use, and thus helps it deliver more accurate playback. And the cleaning gel pot is designed to remove stubborn residue that the cleaning brush can’t get. read more $89 at Goldring Apple Apple MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display This is the first MacBook with a touchscreen display, and it’s designed to sit at the top of Apple’s high-end MacBook Pro range. The MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display features the best and brightest display of any Apple laptop. It also features the best built-in speaker system, a thinner and lighter design (compared to other current MacBook Pros), and is the first MacBook to support the Dynamic Island. read more $2,899 at Apple (14-inch) $3,399 at Apple (16-inch) Musical Fidelity Musical Fidelity Bx1cd CD Player The Bx1cd is a CD player designed to pair with Musical Fidelity’s B1xi integrated stereo amplifier, as both share the same retro-inspired aesthetic. It features a high-quality ESS DAC that plays new audio CDs and older Red Book CDs. It does not support Super Audio CDs (SACDs) or have any kind of built-in streaming capabilities. According to the brand, the B1xcd is “designed in true Musical Fidelity high-end philosophy [and] available at a more accessible price.” read more $799 at Musical Fidelity Apple Apple iPad mini (2026) Two years after its last refresh, Apple has released an improved version of its smallest tablet. This 8th-generation iPad mini is the first to feature an OLED display, so that its screen can get almost twice as bright as the previous model (now up to 1,200 nits). It features Apple’s A20 Pro chip, just like the iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro, promising a “huge leap” in performance. And it’s the first iPad mini to have an IP67 rating. Other features include a slimmer and lighter design and improved speakers. The starting price is $699, which is $200 more than its 2024-released predecessor. read more $699 at Apple Apple Apple 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 Apple has introduced a 14‑inch MacBook Pro for 2026, and the big upgrade over its predecessors is the chip. Apple’s latest-gen models now feature its M6 processor, which the brand promises will deliver a big boost in performance over last year’s M5 models; specifically, the M6 Pros aim to deliver 30 percent faster graphics and 25 percent faster AI workloads. Additionally, battery life has been improved to “up to 24 hours” on a single charge. The design of the 14-inch MacBook Pro remains the same and comes in two colors: space black and silver. read more Starts at $1,999 JBL JBL Classic L150 The JBL L150 Classic is the new flagship floorstanding speaker in the brand’s Classic Series, which features retro designs with modern drivers, crossovers, and acoustics. The speakers have a walnut wood veneer cabinet and come with the brand’s signature black Quadrex foam grilles that magnetically attach. According to JBL, the L150 Classic “brings large-format JBL sound to a wider audience while remaining true to the engineering principles that define the brand.” read more $9,999 at JBL Amazon Amazon Echo Time Amazon’s Echo Time is a smart speaker with a built-in display, designed specifically to sit on your nightstand. In essence, it’s the company’s new smart alarm clock. It features a 3.2-inch circular touchscreen that you can customize with different clock faces. The display can also adapt throughout the day, mimicking a natural sunrise in the morning and gradually dimming in the evening. It comes in three finishes: Graphite, Glacier White and Coral Pink. A matching adjustable stand is also available for $40. read more $200 at Amazon Amazon Amazon Echo Dot (2026) Amazon has refreshed its smallest smart speaker for 2026. The new Echo Dot looks like its predecessor but features an upgraded speaker, a better microphone, and a new AZ3 processor; the result is a better-sounding Echo Dot that can also handle faster, more natural conversations with Alexa+. Additionally, for those invested in Amazon’s smart home ecosystem, the new Echo Dot functions as a smart home hub for Zigbee, Thread and Matter. It also works as an Eero Wi-Fi extender. Available in four colors: graphite, glacier white, agave green and coral pink. read more $100 at Amazon Amazon Amazon Echo Show 16 (2026) Amazon’s new and improved Echo Show 16 is a 16-inch smart display like its predecessor, but it’s prettier, with significantly slimmer bezels and an optional Nanomatte (anti-glare) finish. It comes integrated with Fire TV, so you can use it as a smart TV to watch movies and shows. It has a number of new smart home tools for family organization. And, like before, it functions as a digital photo frame. The Echo Show 16 is designed to hang on the wall, but Amazon sells two optional stands for $70 (regular) and $125 (tilts). read more Starts at $500 Amazon Amazon Echo Studio with Home Camera Amazon has unleashed a new version of its biggest and best-sounding smart speaker. As its name gives away, the all-new Echo Studio with Home Camera has a built-in camera that allows it to double as a smart home camera for your home; you can get a live feed in the Alexa app. As for the Alexa-powered smart speaker, it’s still optimized for playing immersive spatial audio with support for Dolby Atmos. Additionally, it has a new room-tuning feature, called Advanced Room Adaptation, so it sounds best for the space that it’s in. It costs $250, which is $30 more than the 2025-released Echo Studio. read more $250 at Amazon Amazon Amazon Alexa Photo Frame The Alexa Photo Frame is Amazon’s first dedicated digital picture frame. It has a 10-inch display and links with Amazon Photos, which Prime subscribers get unlimited storage for, to show off your photos. It even supports Alexa+, which you can ask to bring up photos of specific friends or family members. It comes in three frame options: black, walnut or birch. The wood options cost $29 more. (Note: Amazon’s existing line of Echo Show smart displays could work as digital picture frames, but it’s not their primary function.) read more $200 at Amazon Audio-Technica Audio-Technica ATH-M50xSTS-WL StreamSet Audio-Technica’s range of StreamSet headsets is designed for content creators, live streamers and podcasters. The ATH-M50xSTS-WL is the first wireless model in the range. They don’t connect via Bluetooth; instead, they use a USB transceiver for an ultra-low-latency connection to PCs or consoles. The headset is modeled after the brand’s ATH-M50x headphones, which sell for around $159. read more $299 at Audio-Technica PlayStation PlayStation Prism Collection The Prism Collection is a transparent line of PlayStation accessories that gives the current PS5 a retro makeover that looks straight out of the late 1990s. It includes DualSense controllers and matching covers for the PS5, each of which is available in three see-through options: Flare Orange, Emerald Green and Graphite Gray. The controllers and console covers will cost $85 and $75, respectively. The collection will officially launch on February 4, 2027. read more Learn More Fujifilm Fujifilm Instax Mini Evo 2 Fujifilm has introduced a second-generation Instax Mini Evo. Like its predecessor, it’s a hybrid digital and instant film camera: it shoots and stores digital photos and has a built-in printer that lets you selectively print them. The Evo 2 adds a larger touchscreen display, which makes it easier to compose photos and adjust settings. It has a new Expanded View feature that gives users a wider field of view than the shooting area. And there’s a new Immersive Movie mode that captures four seconds of video leading up to each photo. read more $290 at Fujifilm Twelve South Twelve South Airfly View The Airfly View is the newest addition to Twelve South’s Airfly range, a line of Bluetooth transmitters that let you use your wireless headphones with an in-flight entertainment system. The difference is that Airfly View is the first one to have a built-in display, which guides you through pairing and confirms when your AirPods (or other wireless headphones) are connected. It also supports two-way Bluetooth, so you can plug it into the auxiliary jack of an older car or boat’s audio system and then stream audio from your smartphone to it. read more $80 at Twelve South $80 at Amazon Apple Apple M6 iMac Apple has upgraded its line of iMac desktop computers for the first time since October 2024. These 2026 editions look identical to their predecessors and come in the same seven vibrant colors. The difference is under the hood, as Apple has equipped each with its M6 processor and faster memory bandwidth. Compared to their M4 predecessors, the new M6 iMacs promise twice as fast graphics and gaming performance, as well as up to 5x faster on-device AI performance (for Apple Intelligence with Siri AI). Starting at $1,499, Apple has kept the price the same as the previous-generation iMacs. read more $1,499 at Apple Audio-Technica Audio-Technica ATH-AWX7000 The Audio-Technica ATH-AWX7000 is the brand’s new flagship pair of closed-back wired headphones. Their most striking feature is gorgeous wooden housings made from Kiso cypress, one of Japan’s finest woods, and hand-finished with Echizen lacquer. But A-T has made sure that they sound as good as they look. Each pair has the brand’s new True Closed-back Acoustic (TCbA) design, which harnesses air pressure generated within the enclosed earcups. They also have new driver technologies that enable the ATH-AWX7000 to reveal “subtle details even within complex and familiar recordings.” read more $3,799 at Audio-Technica Grado Grado Signature S150 Grado’s Signature S150 is the most affordable pair of open-back wired headphones in the brand’s high-end Signature series. It retains Grado’s “signature” retro aesthetic that combines metal components with a gorgeous leather headband and plush ear cushions. It features a new 44mm S driver with a paper-composite diaphragm that Grado says is based on technology used in the larger 52mm S drivers in its HP100 SE ($2,495) and S950 ($2,195) headphones. According to the brand, the S150 “delivers a level of clarity and detail that challenges expectations for a headphone in its class, while preserving the natural body and musical character of the performance.” read more $295 at Grado Schiit Audio Schiit Mani 3 The Mani 3 is the latest evolution of Schiit Audio’s entry-level phono preamplifier, which was last updated in 2022. Like its predecessors, the Mani 3 supports MM and MC cartridges and offers four switchable gain modes, allowing it to work with a wide range of turntables. Compared to the Mani 2, the Mani 3 improves usability with front panel controls for input and gain. Schiit has improved the inner workings of the Mani 3 so that it offers better performance (“by a bit, not a mile”). According to the brand, the Mani 3 offers “the highest performance and flexibility of any affordable phono preamp.” read more $149 at Schiit Audio Esoteric Esoteric Grandioso K1XE The Esoteric Grandioso K1XE is the brand’s new flagship CD player and the newest addition to Esoteric’s high-end Grandioso range of hi-fi components. It can play both CDs and Super Audio CDs (SACDs). It’s equipped with the latest generation of its Master SoundDiscrete DAC G2. that employs a fully dual-mono configuration and incorporates five independent linear power supply systems. It also features Esoteric’s proprietary SACD transport mechanism, VRDS-ATLAS, which is built on an exceptionally rigid, heavy-duty platform. The company claims the Grandioso K1XE represents the pinnacle of all-in-one Super Audio CD/DAC performance and “embodies both the present and future of high-end digital audio.” read more $45,000 at Esoteric Technics Technics SL-1210MKX The Technics SL-1210MKX is the new flagship model in the iconic audio maker’s SL-1200 series of DJ-focused turntables (and the next evolution of the 2019-released SL-1210MK7). It has a significantly heavier chassis, newly designed isolation feet and, for the first time in a SL-1200 series turntable, the SL-1210MKX introduces a dedicated ±4% pitch range. According to the brand, the SL-1210MKX is “designed to address the challenges DJs face in high-pressure performance settings where powerful sound systems, deep bass, structural vibration, and extended operating periods place exceptional demands on equipment.” read more at Technics Linn Linn 343 Compact Loudspeaker System Linn’s 343 is a high-end active floorstanding loudspeaker system that sits just below the Scottish hi-fi manufacturer’s flagship 360 system, which costs $95,915. Each Linn 343 loudspeaker has a four-way design, with the bass driver units powered by the brand’s Pistonik motor system, which is derived from its flagship 360 system. Linn sells the 343 in two distinct models. The “Exakt Integrated” version is fully active system, with a module that houses the power supply, DAC, digital crossover and amplification; it starts at $97,000. The “Passive with Active Bass (PWAB)” version lets you choose the external amplification for the tweeter, midrange and upper bass units; it starts at $67,500. read more Starts at $67,500 Amazon Blink Mini 4K+ For 2026, Amazon has introduced five new Blink smart home security cameras , including a trail camera, two outdoor cameras and the first pan-tilt-zoom camera. The standout of the new additions, however, is the Blink Mini 4K+ as it’s the brand’s first 4K smart home camera. It also supports two-way audio and smart alerts with person and vehicle detection (available with a compatible Blink subscription plan). Available in black or white finishes. read more $80 at Amazon Canor Audio Canor Crius H5S Canor Audio is a Slovakian maker of high-end audio gear. Its Crius H5S is a 3-in-1 hi-fi component comprised of a headphone amplifier, DAC and preamplifier. It features a dual-mono ES9039Q2M DAC paired with a fully discrete architecture and balanced analog output stages. According to the brand, it can drive highly sensitive IEMs or demanding high-impedance planar magnetic headphones. It also includes optical, coaxial, and USB inputs, connecting to a wide range of digital sources. It’s built with premium materials such as high-grade aluminum, steel and glass. It comes in three finishes: black, silver, or bronze. At the time of writing, US pricing and availability haven’t been released. read more Learn More Audiolab Audiolab PPA7 Phono Preamplifier The PPA7 is the first standalone phono preamplifier that the British hi-fi company has released in nearly 20 years. It’s a high-performance phono preamplifier that, according to the brand, is “designed to bring greater clarity, control and versatility to vinyl playback.” It’s compatible with both moving-magnet (MM) and moving-coil (MC) cartridges, and has selectable load options for both. Interestingly, the PPA7 also has a dedicated headphone amplifier and a Bluetooth transmitter, allowing you to enjoy a private listening session or stream audio to your wireless headphones or speakers. read more $699 at Audiolab Triangle Hi-Fi Triangle Borea BR05 Triangle’s Borea BR05 is a pair of passive standmount loudspeakers with a two-way design. Each speaker features a newly designed 21cm midwoofer paired with the brand’s 25mm silk-dome EFS (Efficient Flow System) tweeter, a signature on all Triangle’s Borea loudspeakers. They are designed around a 9-driver tribrid architecture, featuring a dynamic driver for low frequencies, balanced armature drivers for mids and highs, and MEMS drivers for ultra-high frequencies. Each earbud is constructed of 6061-T6 aluminum. According to Astell&Kern, the Clarus is designed to deliver transparent and distortion-free audio exactly as the artist intended. At the time of writing, price and availability info have not yet been released. read more Shop Now Noble Audio Noble Audio Osprey The Osprey is the newest and most affordable addition to the Texas-based brand’s wireless earbud offerings. Each Osprey earbud features a hybrid dual-driver configuration that pairs a 10mm dynamic driver with a custom-balanced armature. According to the brand, this combo “provides confident, controlled bass, a natural and expressive midrange, and clean, extended highs with excellent separation.” The earbuds support LDAC and thus can stream high-resolution audio over Bluetooth. And they feature active noise-cancellation and transparency modes. read more $199 at Noble Audio $199 at Audio46 Astell&Kern Astell&Kern SP4000T The Astell&Kern SP4000T is the next evolution of the company’s flagship portable hi-fi player. As the “T” indicates, its main upgrade is the integration of four vacuum tubes. Specifically, the SP4000T features Raytheon JAN6418 MIL-Spec vintage vacuum tubes in a quad configuration. It also features a new Triple Tube Mode that lets listeners choose from up to 54 combinations of tube and amp current settings, allowing them to fully customize their sound. At the time of writing, pricing hasn’t been announced, but you can expect it to go for north of $4,290, which was the current SP4000 is going for. read more Learn More Learn More Sony Sony Bravia 9 II True RGB TV The Bravia 9 II is the company’s flagship Mini LED TV for 2026. Sony calls it a “True RGB” TV because it’s integrated with its proprietary RGB backlighting technology, which individually controls each red, green, and blue LED, helping it deliver the most vibrant, color-accurate picture. Naturally, this technology comes at a price. The TVs come in 65-inch to 115-inch sizes, which range from $3,600 to $31,000. (Note: Sony has also introduced a more affordable True RGB TV in the Bravia 7 II.) read more Starts at $3,600 Fiio Fiio Level 1 Fiio’s Level 1 is an integrated amplifier that combines a power amplifier, preamplifier and DAC, as well as both wired and wireless connections, into one compact box that weighs just 1.49 pounds. The amplifier can deliver up to 300 watts per channel (at 4 ohms), which should be more than enough to handle most bookshelf speakers and desktop monitors (and even less demanding floorstanding speakers). And it boasts numerous wired and wireless connections, so you can hook it up to a laptop or desktop, as well as traditional hi-fi sources. read more $140 at Apos Sennheiser Sennheiser Momentum 5 Wireless The Sennheiser Momentum 5 Wireless is the company’s new flagship pair of wireless ANC headphones for 2026. They look quite similar to their predecessors, the 2022-released Momentum 4 Wireless, and even boast the same 42mm transducers, but the company is promising vastly improved performance for the Momentum 5 Wireless. They can play higher-resolution audio and support Dolby Atmos with head-tracking. Thanks to a more advanced processor and more built-in mics, they should have much better ANC and far superior call quality. Maybe most interestingly, the built-in battery is now user-replaceable (with a Phillips-head screwdriver), which should greatly extend the headphones’ lifespan. Available in black, white and blue finishes. read more $400 at Sennheiser Tidal Audio Tidal Piano Classic Tidal Audio claims that the Piano Classic is a “reinterpretation” of the brand’s original loudspeakers, the 1999-released Piano, as it has the same basic construction and is built with the same design principles. However, it’s been upgraded with new tech and materials. According to the brand, the Piano Classic “comes with the DNA fingerprint of what Tidal is all about: building timeless masterpieces with the unique, crystal clear, and naturally pure sound.” read more $31,990 at Tidal Audio Sony Sony Bravia Theater Trio Sony’s Bravia Theater Trio is a set of three speakers: one compact soundbar and two side speakers. It’s positioned as the perfect middle ground between a one-box soundbar and a stereo system, as it’s able to deliver the crisp dialogue of a soundbar along with the wide, immersive soundstage that typically comes from a stereo pair. The three speakers are designed to work with Sony’s latest Bravia TVs, as they support Direct Connect (which allows wireless connection). The system supports the latest immersive technologies, including Dolby Atmos, DTS:X and IMAX Enhanced. Additionally, the Bravia Theater Trio can be expanded into a true surround sound system by integrating Sony’s wireless satellite speakers and subwoofers. read more $2,200 at Sony Luxman Luxman D-100 Centennial Luxman’s D-100 Centennial is effectively a new and improved version of the company’s previous flagship CD player, the D-10X, which it has been selling since 2020 and costs around $16,500. Like its predecessor, it can play both CDs and SACDs. However, Luxman has made wholesale changes, completely rebuilding its disc drive, digital circuitry and analog output stage all from the ground up. According to the brand, it marks “a significant evolution in flagship disc-player performance.” read more $18,995 at All Elite Audio Andover Audio Andover Audio Andover-One MK2 The Andover One MK2 is the brand’s new flagship all-in-one turntable, built in the same image as its 2020 predecessor. It’s built with the same IsoGroove technology, which is a mechanical structure that effectively eliminates most unwanted vibrations. And it’s a complete one-box, hi-fi system that supports Bluetooth streaming (when not listening to vinyl). However, the MK2 has been upgraded with new refinements to improve its sound, usability and integration with other audio systems that you may already have in your home. read more $2,699 at Andover Audio Dali Dali Vega Dali’s Vega is the brand’s first all-in-one wireless speaker system. It features 10 in-house-developed drivers backed by 400 watts of amplification. Additionally, it’s integrated with Dali’s proprietary Adaptive Stereo Enhancement (ASE) technology, which helps it create a wider, more expansive soundstage than you’d expect from a single speaker. The Vega supports Bluetooth and Wi-Fi streaming, as well as a wide range of wired connections (so you can use it as a speaker for your turntable or TV). According to the brand, the Vega “redefines what is possible from a single-box wireless sound system.” read more $4,500 at Dali Bang & Olufsen Bang & Olufsen Beosystem 9000c (Fragment Edition) Bang & Olufsen teamed up with Fragment Design, one of Japan’s most influential design brands, to create a special-edition version of the Beosystem 9000c that was released in 2024. It’s the same music system as before, comprising a refurbished version of the brand’s iconic Beosystem 9000 CD player, paired with a set of the brand’s Beolab 28 wireless speakers. This special-edition version features matte-black surfaces with glossy natural aluminum and adds Fragment’s distinctive lightning bolt logo. While the original costs $55K, this model is considerably more expensive. read more $69,500 at Bang & Olufsen Sony Sony 1000X The ColleXion Sony’s 1000X The ColleXion is the brand’s new flagship pair of noise-canceling headphones, released to celebrate the 10-year anniversary of the first 1000X Series headphones, the MDR-1000X, introduced in 2026. You can think of these new models as a more luxurious version of the 1000XM6,as they are similar in the vast majority of ways but are made with more premium materials, including soft vegan leather and metal accents. Sony says they “represent the most refined expression of Sony’s headphone design, combining premium materials, refined craftsmanship, and exceptional comfort.” read more $650 at Sony Schiit Audio Schiit Audio Vestri The Vestri is a portable DAC and headphone amplifier that connects to your smartphone, laptop or tablet via USB-C and makes your wired headphones sound way better. It’s notable for a few reasons. First, the Schiit Audio’s first-ever portable hi-fi gadget. Secondly, it’s different from other portable DAC/amps because it’s integrated with the brand’s exclusive Mesh conversion technology, which combines a time- and frequency-domain-optimized digital filter with an on-board DAC. According to Schiit, this results in “sonic performance far above its peers.” read more $99 at Schiit Audio Campfire Audio Campfire Audio Chimera The Chimera is the Portland-based audio maker’s most high-end and expensive pair of in-ear monitors. Each earbud features a unique nine-driver architecture that combines four distinct driver technologies: dynamic, balanced armature, electrostatic and bone conduction. (In fact, it’s the first time Campfire Audio has incorporated a conduction driver and embedded it directly into its CNC-machined magnesium shell.) The result, according to the brand, “is a listening experience that is both highly detailed and physically engaging.” The Chimera ships with an ALO Audio Valence-6 cable featuring four high-purity copper conductors and two 50/50 copper-silver-plated conductors. read more $7,500 at Campfire Audio Denon Denon AVR-X2900H The Denon AVR-X2900H is an advanced AV receiver in the company’s midrange X-Series; it’s quite similar to the Denon AVR-X3900H, but slightly less powerful and supports fewer channels. It’s a 7.2-channel AVR that can deliver up to 95 watts (at 8 ohms) per channel. Denon describes it as “a clear step up for home theater enthusiasts ready to move beyond entry-level sound.” read more $1,349 at Denon Denon Denon AVR-X3900H Denon’s AVR-X3900H is one of the most advanced AV receivers in the brand’s midrange X-Series. It’s a 9.4-channel AVR that’s capable of delivering up to 105 watts (at 8 ohms) per channel. It has four independent subwoofer outputs, too, making it geared towards more advanced home theaters and professionally designed systems. According to the brand, it’s designed for those who “want more power, more precision, and more control from their home theater systems.” read more $1,849 at Denon Fosi Audio Fosi Audio MD3 MagDAC The MD3 MagDAC is a portable DAC and headphone amplifier that magnetically snaps to the back of your iPhone. It pairs an ESS ES9039Q2M DAC chipset with four ESS ES9603 headphone amplifier chips in a true balanced circuit design. It features both 3.5 mm (single-ended) and 4.4 mm (balanced) headphone outputs, offering up to 180 mW of output power via the balanced connection. And there’s a 1.28-inch LCD touchscreen for adjusting settings; plus, users can upload custom images to display and add some personal flair. According to the brand, the MD3 MagDAC is “designed for listeners seeking high-quality wired audio wherever they go.” read more $150 at Fosi Audio Noble Audio Noble Audio FoKus Apollo Pro Noble Audio has introduced a higher-end (or “Pro”) version of its FoKus Apollo wireless noise-canceling headphones, released in late 2024 and priced at $649. The FoKus Apollo Pro are quite similar to its non-Pro siblings, featuring the same unique hybrid driver (dynamic and planar magnetic) arrangement and the same active noise-canceling technology. The primary difference with the Pro headphones is that they’re made with higher-end materials, including fabric finishes, revised gunmetal accents and upgraded fabric cabling. The brand hasn’t specified how many, but claims that only a “limited-run” of the Apollo Pro will be released. read more $699 at Bloom Audio Marshall Marshall Milton A.N.C Marshall’s Milton A.N.C is a pair of on-ear active noise-canceling headphones. Just like the brand’s other offerings, these headphones are designed in the same image as its iconic guitar amps: all-black with brass details. Other than this signature look, the Milton A.N.C. boasts an impressive “up to 50-hour” battery life with ANC turned on (or 80 hours with ANC off). They are also “Find My” compatible with both Apple’s and Google’s smartphones. At $280, they’re the company’s most affordable noise-canceling headphones that it sells. read more $230 at Marshall Wharfedale Wharfedale Denton 1S Wharfedale’s Denton 1S are new, reimagined versions of the company’s original Denton 1 bookshelf speakers, which were released in 1974. Like the originals, the Denton 1S have a modern design (curved cabinets) and a unique coaxial driver, which positions the tweeter inside the mid-woofer unit, making it appear like a single driver. But each speaker has been re-engineered from the ground up. According to the brand, they reinterpret “what a compact, modern hi-fi loudspeaker can be.” read more $999 at Wharfedale USA (Pair) Wrensilva Wrensilva Studio Wrensilva’s Studio is a modern record console that’s essentially a smaller (and more affordable) version of the company’s previous record consoles, including the $19,000 M1 and $15,000 The Standard. It’s an all-in-one hi-fi system that can play your favorite vinyl records and stream your favorite music over Wi-Fi (via Sonos multiroom) or Bluetooth. It’s also a beautifully designed statement piece. read more $9,900 at Wrensilva $10,800 at Wrensilva (w/ Sonos) Sony Sony A7R VI The Sony A7R VI is the company’s highest-resolution mirrorless camera to date. It features a fully stacked, full-frame 67-megapixel sensor (making it the first A7R model to have a fully-stacked sensor) with up to 16 stops of dynamic range. Paired with a faster Bionz XR2 processor, the company claims that it results in “exceptional resolution, accurate color, and reliable performance across subjects ranging from people in motion to wildlife to expansive landscapes.” read more $4,500 at Sony (Body Only) Audio-Technica Audio-Technica AT-VM95EBK The Audio-Technica AT-VM95EBK is the newest addition to the brand’s VM95 series of entry-level phono cartridges. In fact, it’s actually the same moving-magnet phono cartridges as the brand’s existing AT-VM95E, but instead of green, it comes in a refined black finish. According to the brand, AT-VM95EBK brings “the proven VM95 Series engineering into a clean black design, featuring a 0.3 x 0.7 mil elliptical stylus and specially wound coils that deliver a 4.0 mV output with excellent channel separation and low distortion.” read more $74 at Audio-Technica $109 at Audio-Technica (Kit) Panasonic Panasonic Lumix L10 Panasonic’s Lumix L10 is a compact fixed-lens camera released to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the Lumix brand. It features the same 20.4-megapixel Micro Four Thirds sensor as in the company’s Lumix GH7. Plus, it packs a hybrid phase-detect autofocus system and comes with a fixed Leica DC Vario-Summilux 24-75mm (f/1.7-2.8) zoom lens. According to the brand, its “tactile controls and balanced design creates a seamless shooting experience, enabling photographers to capture moments freely, without distraction, particularly suited for street, travel and everyday photography.” read more $1,500 at Panasonic Shanling Shanling EC Play The Shanling EC Play is a new-age Discman built in the same vein as the brand’s other portable speakers. According to the brand, it “combines the nostalgia of CDs with modern wireless and high-resolution audio features.” Its main “modern” feature is support for two-way Bluetooth. So if you don’t want to use wired headphones, it can stream music to your wireless headphones or a Bluetooth speaker. read more $199 at Shanling Garmin Garmin Forerunner 70 and Forerunner 170 Garmin’s Forerunner 70 and Forerunner 170 are the brand’s new entry-level running watches for 2026 (they replace Forerunner 55 and Forerunner 165). The two models look identical, featuring the same 43mm case, 1.2-inch AMOLED touchscreen display, and five physical buttons. And both have the same sensors and support the same 80+ exercises (both individual workouts and team sports). That said, the Forerunner 170 is the slightly higher-end model. It adds NFC (for mobile payments), a built-in altimeter (for more accurate elevation tracking), and Garmin’s more advanced coaching features. On the flip side, the Forerunner 70 has slightly better battery life, which lasts up to 13 days (versus 10 days). read more $250 at Garmin (Forerunner 70) $300 at Garmin (Forerunner 170) Yamaha Yamaha RX300A The Yamaha RX300A is a 5.2-channel AV receiver that’s the direct successor to the company’s previous entry-level model, the RX-V385, but boasts a fresh look (a cleaner front panel with fewer buttons) and contemporary features, including support for flexible Dolby Atmos speaker configurations. According to the brand, this includes “3.2.2-channel with up-firing or in-ceiling height speakers, as well as 5.2-channel with virtual height processing.” read more $400 at Yamaha $400 at Adorama Yamaha Yamaha RX500A The Yamaha RX500A is an entry-level AV receiver that’s positioned as the “next step up” from the company’s RX300A. It looks almost identical, but delivers more power, supports Wi-Fi streaming and supports a more complex surround-sound system. It’s a 7.2‑channel AV receiver that can support in‑ceiling, up‑firing, and virtual layouts. read more $600 at Yamaha $600 at Adorama Canon Canon EOS R6 V Canon EOS R6 V is the company’s first full-frame camera that’s squarely aimed at vloggers. It inherits the same 32.5-megapixel sensor used in the EOS R6 III ($2,799), as well as the same 7K/60p RAW video shooting capabilities. However, it lacks the electronic viewfinder in favor of a lighter design. According to the brand, the R6 V is “designed for creatives who capture video on a daily basis who want control, operability, and reliability, with limited creative constraints.” read more $2,499 at Canon (Body Only) Twelve South Twelve South PowerClip Twelve South’s PowerClip is a ultracompact portable power bank that’s about the size of an AirPods Pro case. It has a 2000mAh capacity, meaning it can charge most smartphones from zero to around 30-percent. It’s also integrated with two USB-C charging cables, one of which supports passthrough power. This means you can use it to draw power from a larger device (like MacBook) to simultaneously recharge the PowerClip and charge a secondary device (like an iPhone). Lastly, it has a built-in ring and an attachable carabiner, so you can clip in onto a keychain or zipper. Twelve South offers the PowerClip in five different colors. read more $40 at Twelve South Bose Bose Lifestyle Ultra Speaker The Bose Lifestyle Ultra Speaker is the company’s new entry-level smart speaker with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth streaming capabilities. It also has an auxiliary jack, so you can use it as a wired speaker with a computer or turntable. As a standalone mono speaker, it features two front-firing and one up-firing driver. For the best stereo experience, you can configure two in a stereo pair. In Sonos terms, it can best be described as a hybrid between the Era 100 ($219) and Era 300 ($449) smart speakers. read more $299 at Bose $349 (14% off) Google Google Fitbit Air The Fitbit Air is a screenless wearable designed in a similar mold to Whoop. Instead of working like an extension of your smartphone, it simply tracks your health metrics and sends them to Google’s all-new Health app (which replaces the Fitbit app). It features multiple sensors (including heart rate, accelerometer/gyroscope, infrared SpO2 and skin temperature) and supports haptic feedback for alarms. As for battery life, Google claims it can last a week on a single charge. Unlike Whoop, the Fitbit Air doesn’t require a subscription. But with one, you get access to an AI-powered health coach, which can help plan customized workout and nutrition plans. read more $99 at Google $99 at Amazon reMarkable reMarkable Paper Pure The reMarkable Paper Pure is the company’s most affordable e-ink tablet to date. As the successor to the 2020-released reMarkable 2, the Paper Pure is a 10.3-inch digital notebook that’s designed to mimic the experience of writing and drawing on paper. It shares similar features to its pricier siblings, in that it comes with an active stylus and boasts a 3-week battery life, but it’s a monochrome tablet so you can’t write or draw in color. read more $399 at reMarkable $449 at Amazon (Bundle) Devialet Devialet Phantom Ultimate (Roland-Garros Exclusive Edition) Ahead of the French Open, Devialet has introduced special-edition versions of its flagship wireless speakers. They’re the same Phantom Ultimate wireless speakers released in fall 2025, but with clay red accents inspired by the tournament’s signature clay courts. Like before, they come in two different versions: the larger Phantom Ultimate 108dB and the smaller Phantom Ultimate 98dB. Naturally, these special-edition versions are a little pricier than the standard models. read more $4,200 at Devialet (108 dB) $2,100 at Devialet (98 dB) Garmin Garmin JL Audio Primacy Garmin acquired JL Audio, an American hi-fi brand known for its in-car and in-boat audio systems, back in 2023. Now, leveraging its expertise, has released a high-end wireless stereo system. The JL Audio Primacy consists of two active speakers (either tower or standmount) and one network streamer. The brand describes it as “a premium home audio system that offers extraordinary sound performance that’s tuned exactly for each listener’s space.” read more $90,000 at Garmin (T6) $35,000 at Garmin (S3) $15,000 at Garmin (CS) Bose Bose Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar The Bose Lifestyle Ultra Soundbar is the company’s new flagship Dolby Atmos soundbar (taking that title from Bose’s Smart Ultra Soundbar, which was released in late 2023 and priced at $999). At $1,099, it’s priced and positioned as a direct rival to Sonos’s current flagship soundbar, the $1,099 Arc Ultra. It’s a 5.2-channel soundbar with nine drivers: four front-facing full-range drivers, two up-firing full-range drivers, a center tweeter and two of Bose’s proprietary PhaseGuide drivers. According to the brand, the Dolby Atmos soundbar is “capable of playing back three-dimensional sound with lifelike realism and a convincing sense of height, all by itself.” read more $1,099 at Bose Bose Bose Lifestyle Ultra Subwoofer The Bose Lifestyle Ultra Subwoofer is the company’s flagship wireless subwoofer for 2026. Priced at $899, it’s a direct rival to the Sonos Sub 4, which costs exactly the same. According to the brand, the Lifestyle Ultra Subwoofer “delivers deep, controlled bass that remains clear at any volume, adding weight and authority for the ultimate home theater experience.” read more $899 at Bose Jamo Jamo Concert Legacy Series The Concert Legacy is the higher-end of Jamo’s two new Concert loudspeaker ranges. It draws inspiration from the original Concert 8 and Concert 11 loudspeakers that were introduced in 1996. According to Jamo, the refreshed line “explores how those classics would have naturally progressed over three decades of innovation.” The range consists of three models: the Concert Legacy 8 bookshelf speakers, the Concert Legacy 9 compact floorstanding speakers, and the flagship Concert Legacy 11 floorstanding speakers. read more $7,999 at Jamo (Legacy 11) $5,299 at Jamo (Legacy 9) $2,999 at Jamo (Legacy 8) Jamo Jamo Concert Element Series The Concert Element is the more affordable and lifestyle-focused of Jamo’s two new Concert ranges of loudspeakers. Developed with HarritSørensen, a Copenhagen-based industrial design firm, the series is characterized by its innovative “The Circle over the Square” architecture. This means that each driver is hidden underneath a circular module that, according to the brand, extends “beyond the shallow rectangular enclosure, making the sound-producing element both the visual and acoustic center of the speaker.” The range consists of four loudspeaker models: the Concert Element 50 bookshelf speakers, the Concert Element 70 compact floorstanding speakers and the flagship Concert Element 90 floorstanding speakers. There’s also a wired subwoofer, the Concert Element SW10. read more $2,499 at Jamo (Element 90) $1,899 at Jamo (Element 70) $1,099 at Jamo (Element 50) $699 at Jamo (Element SW10) DJI DJI Osmo Mobile 8P The Osmo Mobile 8P is a higher-end version of the Osmo Mobile 8 that DJI released in November 2025. Like its non-P sibling, the 8P is a three-axis handheld gimbal that helps creators capture stabilized videos with their iPhone. The 8P has a few upgraded features, but the standout is its detachable remote control with a built-in screen. This screen mirrors the view from your iPhone and lets creators more easily record themselves away from the gimbal when it’s standing on its built-in tripod. The catch? Like many of DJI’s latest gadgets, it doesn’t have a US price or release date at this time. read more Learn More Audiovector Audiovector R5 Arreté Audiovector’s R5 Arreté is a pair of high-end floorstanding loudspeakers that, according to the brand, are the first models in the R Series to carry technologies inherited directly from its flagship $165,000 R10 Arreté loudspeakers. Each loudspeaker has a 3.5-way design and packs the same tweeter and midrange drivers as the R10 Arreté, but just doesn’t have as many of them (or any long-throw bass drivers). So you’re getting a loudspeaker with many of the same technologies, but in a smaller and more affordable package. read more $24,400 at Audiovector Schiit Audio Schiit Buf Schiit Audio’s Buf is a tube buffer that’s designed to be placed between your preamplifier and power amplifier, or between your DAC and integrated amplifier (or preamp or headphone amplifier) in your hi-fi system. The idea is that the audio signal passes through the Buf, which adds warm tones typically associated with vacuum tubes to an otherwise sterile sound. Is it necessary? No, but it’s fun. According to Schiit, you should consider the Buf if you’re bored with your system’s sound or just want to experiment with the warmth of vacuum tubes. read more $99 at Schiit Audio About the Author: Tucker Bowe has been on Gear Patrol’s editorial team since 2014. With a passion for consumer tech and hi-fi, he tracks everything from headphones and turntables to smartphones and wearables. If it lights up or makes noise, he probably covers it.

title: Yeti Just Brought Back Its Awesomely Overbuilt Garage and Man-Cave Grail
summary: The Can Crusher sold out quickly upon release last year. It gets a one-off restock just in time for gifting season.
content: The Can Crusher sold out quickly upon release last year. It gets a one-off restock just in time for gifting season. Yeti If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more For many Americans, Thanksgiving weekend means pumpkin desserts, football and a lot of rare Yeti gear. Every year, the brand ushers in the holiday season with something it calls Gear Garage, which sees both one-off variations of best-sellers and restocks on fan favorites. For 2026, that means the return of its awesomely overbuilt garage grail. Say hello, once again, to the Can Crusher . The Can Crusher is back for the first time in over a year. Yeti A smash hit First launched in 2025, the Can Crusher sold out quickly upon release, making this restock of particular note for longtime and first-time Yeti fans who missed out last year. The Can Crusher follows the form factor of other Yeti gear. It’s powder-coated to resist rust and weighs more than five pounds. The Can Crusher weighs more than five pounds and operates via a one-hand lever. Yeti Yeti says it handles standard 12-ounce cans as well as taller 16-ounce tallboys. Mounted to the wall, the lever mechanism is designed for single-handed operation, and the construction carries the same overbuilt aesthetic Yeti applies across its drinkware and cooler lineup. As we noted last year , it is the kind of thing that earns a spot in a well-appointed garage precisely because it looks like it belongs there alongside serious equipment rather than a dollar-store impulse buy. It comes with hardware to install in minutes. Yeti Availability and pricing One of several drops happening during Gear Garage, the Can Crusher is exclusively available as part of a box set that also includes engraved 12-ounce Colsters and a beer-themed hat. It costs $200. (The Can Crusher originally sold for $125 last year.) The box set also includes a hat with a new beer-themed patch. Yeti The included Colsters hold 12-ounce cans. Yeti The other boxes, sold separately, include coffee accessories made in collaboration with Onyx Coffee Lab, cookware and a unique dog toy. Yeti Yeti Beer Gift Box $200 at Yeti About the Author: Jack Seemer is the executive editor at Gear Patrol, with over a decade of experience in product journalism. title: Nike ACG Reimagines Camo with Its New Technical Fleece
summary: The ACG Wolf Tree Jacket features an alluring camo print that will have you simultaneously standing out and blending in.
content: The ACG Wolf Tree Jacket features an alluring camo print that will have you simultaneously standing out and blending in. Nike If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more Try imagining camouflage prints, and the typical wooded variety most likely comes to mind. While Mossy Oak and Realtree have seen massive jumps in popularity in the last few years with the lifestyle set, there are many more underrated patterns that frankly, look even cooler than your typical camo. Nike ACG proves that point with its latest fleece, an alluring and comfortable midlayer designed with a stylized print inspired by the brand’s home state. The Mystic Dates/Black/Summit White colorway of the new ACG Wolf Tree Full-Zip Printed Jacket show off the brand’s unique take on camo, courtesy of native Oregon landscapes. Nike As an Oregon native, Nike and its steadily-growing outdoor sub-label have an intimate knowledge of the PNW state’s natural environments, which have inspired the latest technical fleece from ACG. The ACG Wolf Tree Full-Zip Printed Jacket wears a brand-unique camo print inspired by Wolf Tree Trail near Oregon’s Smith Rock. As non-traditional as the pattern is, applied to the classic fleece silhouette, its almost tortoiseshell aesthetic looks right at home. The ACG Wolf Tree Jacket is built using Polartec fleece, a 100-percent polyester material known for its premium warmth and ultrasoft feel. Polartec’s composition helps retain body heat while letting moisture escape, making it an ideal fabric for hiking and outdoor exploration. While Nike ACG and its latest layer are rooted in all-conditions adventure, the new jacket is equally suited to urban exploration, thanks to its loose-fit styling and unique look. The ACG Wolf Tree Jacket is available in unisex sizing with an XS-XXL size run, and is priced at $140. title: Titaner’s Tiny, Ultralight Titanium EDC Utility Knife Punches Well Above Its Weight
summary: At just over 1.0 ounce, this sci-fi-inspired cutting tool is so absurdly lightweight, you might forget it's in your pocket.
content: At just over 1.0 ounce, this sci-fi-inspired cutting tool is so absurdly lightweight, you might forget it’s in your pocket. Titaner If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more I’ve said it before, and I’ll say it again: everyday carry is a game of ounces, sometimes grams. Your pockets can only bear so much weight, and the lighter you can keep your loadout, the less bogged down you’ll feel throughout the day. Of course, that shouldn’t come at the expense of capability and quality. And that is precisely what makes Titaner’s Voidark EDC utility knife such an interesting prospect: it puts high strength, durability and precision-cutting power into an incredibly lightweight package. The Voidark measures only 10 centimeters long and weighs just over an ounce. Titaner Pocket starship If you’re familiar with Titaner as a brand, you know it has a flair for sci-fi-inspired gear. The Voidark is certainly no exception, boasting the same futuristic overall design as the majority of the brand’s other offerings. There’s also a bit of cheekiness to that styling, as it is suggestive of the brand’s forward-thinking designs and construction materials. And like its predecessors, the Voidark boasts the brand’s go-to material, titanium, in abundance. The main body of this utility knife is made entirely of titanium (a single, unbroken piece, too), which is extremely strong but also lightweight. In fact, the entire tool weighs about 30 grams, just a hair over an ounce (1.05 ounces, to be exact). It also measures just 10 centimeters long, which is about 3.94 inches. The body is made from a single, solid piece of ultralight, super-strong titanium. Titaner Despite that absurdly low weight and small size (so low, I’d imagine you could forget you’re even carrying it), it’s still incredibly strong and durable. And we haven’t even gotten to its functionality yet. Slender slicer You’ve probably noticed that this doesn’t look like a standard utility knife. Rather than traditional blades, this one takes any standard 9-millimeter snap-off blade, thereby lowering downtime when the blade gets dull, offering quick access to a new edge and keeping replacement costs down. In fact, it even has its own built-in blade snapper, making it even more convenient. The slider features an integrated lock that’s as easy to operate as it is secure and reliable. Titaner The knife operates via an integrated slider with its own built-in lock. To engage the blade, push down on the slider. Then, while maintaining pressure, push the slider forward. It’s as simple as it is secure and reliable. It’s also quick and easy to replace the blade. Remember the removable blade snapper? It’s also a tail piece that, when removed, allows access to swap in a new blade. And it’s manageable in seconds flat. And that’s to say nothing of the integrated tritium slots, multiple color and finish options, upgradability to a full titanium edition (which swaps the rear aluminum plate for titanium) and more. It’s a different take on an EDC utility knife, but an impressive one nonetheless. Titaner Pricing and availability The Titaner Voidark EDC utility knife is now funding on Kickstarter, and it has already well exceeded its goal, so it’s going into production. You can secure one for yourself now, starting at $85 (down from the $152 MSRP). title: This Serious Integrated Sports Watch Gets a Stunning New Moonphase Dial
summary: Bell & Ross outfits the BR-05 integrated sports watch with a new moonphase complication that delivers a realistic depiction.
content: Fly me to the Moon and let me play among the stars. Bell & Ross If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more Bell & Ross is a luxury tool watch brand heavily inspired by aeronautical engineering, most notably with its signature rounded-square case featuring four exposed screws, modeled after an airplane instrument panel. But the French watchmaker is also obsessed with space. Its newest creation brings a moonphase to the brand’s flagship BR-05 collection for the first time, presented in a typically innovative fashion. The BR-05 Moonphase brings the lunar complication to the BR-05 collection for the first time. Bell & Ross The new BR-05 Moonphase utilizes the collection’s standard integrated sports watch iteration of Bell & Ross’s rounded-square case. Measuring 40mm, the stainless steel is finished with satin-brushed surfaces and mirror-polished chamfers. The H-link stainless steel bracelet features a matching satin-brushed finish and polished center links, with a tapered shape and a butterfly folding clasp. The watch is also available on a black rubber strap with a matching taper and a stainless steel clasp. The BR-05 Moonphase features a 40mm stainless steel case. Bell & Ross Like the BR-05 Blue Diamond Eagle released earlier this year, the dial plate is made of solid aventurine glass, creating a shimmer that resembles a starry night sky. The skinny stick-style hour and minute hands (there is no seconds hand) and indices are borrowed from the BR-05 Grey Mirror Steel , released in 2025, which features a rhodium-plated mirror polish. The moonphase at 6:00 is cut out of an aventurine glass dial plate. Bell & Ross The completely original aspect of this design is, as previously stated, the moonphase. Placed at 6:00, it dominates the dial with an oversized round aperture, displaying a novel representation of the lunar cycle. As the brand describes it, “the Moon’s craters are reproduced on a sapphire crystal plate using a grey PVD coating, partially removed by laser to create different shades of grey and recreate the details of its surface.” The stationary, photorealistic depiction of the moon also features blue-emitting Super-LumiNova. Bell & Ross A semi-transparent disc rotates beneath the dial plate to represent the eight stages of the lunar cycle. Rather than fully obscuring the moon, as a traditional moonphase does, this method reproduces the shadow cast on the lunar surface facing away from the sun. This intricate design honors the fact that the entire Moon is always there in the night sky. We can only ever see the portions that the Sun’s light hits each night. The caseback features an engraving of the Moon. Bell & Ross This realistic interpretation of a moonphase complication is powered by a Bell & Ross Caliber BR.330 automatic movement, with the rotating shadow plate driven by the hour hand. It beats at 4Hz and provides a 65-hour power reserve. Availability and price The Bell & Ross BR-05 Moonphase is available now for $6,300 on a stainless steel bracelet and $5,800 on a black rubber strap. It joins the regular production BR-05 collection. title: Citizen Drops a a Seriously Impressive Root Beer GMT Watch
summary: Thanks to this unusual material combination, one of the brand's best mechanical timepieces just got way more interesting.
content: Thanks to this unusual material combination, one of the brand’s best mechanical timepieces just got way more interesting. Citizen If you buy from a link, we may earn a commission. Learn more Damascus steel has a long history in swordmaking, but it’s not exactly something you expect to find on a wristwatch. While still relatively uncommon in the industry, Damascus steel has nevertheless popped up with relatively more frequency over the past few years. Now, Citizen has found a rather interesting new use for the material, incorporating its distinctive, wavy pattern into the case of its latest Series8 GMT. Citizen celebrates the 5th anniversary of the Series8 revival with a gold-toned Damascus steel version of the GMT model. Citizen A true GMT The Series8 880 GMT is one of the more interesting watches in Citizen’s mechanical lineup. It’s essentially the brand’s take on a contemporary luxury sport GMT with an integrated-bracelet design, angular multi-piece case, textured dials and strong magnetic resistance. And seeing that it houses a “true” GMT movement, you can independently adjust the hour hand for local time. 2026 marks the fifth anniversary of the higher-end Series 8 revamp, and the watchmaker is celebrating the occasion by experimenting with materials. The material is subtly used on the case’s center strip. Plus, forged carbon is employed for the dial. Citizen Gold(-tone) standard For the task, it employs a gold-tone stainless steel case with a subtle Damascus steel strip in the center section. The overt nature of the material doesn’t stand out too much, integrating well amidst the rest of the gold coloring on the housing and bezel. Visible through the caseback, the in-house automatic movement is a true GMT allowing you to independently adjust the local hour hand. Citizen The watch is paired with a gray calfskin leather strap. Citizen If the Damascus gold isn’t enough, Citizen has also decided to play around with forged carbon on the dial. Pairing two materials with very different use cases and histories makes for a decidedly modern-looking timepiece. Atop the case, a stylish root beer bezel ties it all together. The rotating 24-hour design is split in half with black marking the top “nighttime” portion and brown covering the lower “daytime” portion. Surprisingly sleek despite being somewhat experimental with its materials, the watch ties its look together with a root beer 24-hour bezel design. Citizen The rest of the specs are the same as before. Water resistant to 100m, the 41mm case houses the in-house Caliber 9054 automatic GMT movement and is adorned with a gray calfskin strap. Price and availability The Series8 880 GMT in Damascus and forged carbon is available now from Citizen’s website. It’s priced at $2,195.
